sections.html:
Guilford has two counters. Greensboro is at 201 W. Market St., with real estate and recording upstairs on the second floor. High Point is at 325 E. Russell Ave., Room 155. One number, 336-641-7556, serves both, and staff work weekdays from 8 until 5.

Mail can be addressed to P.O. Box 3427, Greensboro, NC 27402, or P.O. Box 1467, High Point, NC 27261. General questions can go to guilforddeeds@guilfordcountync.gov. One set of land records covers a Jamestown farmhouse, a Summerfield lot and a downtown Greensboro condo alike.

Deliver a properly formatted deed with the recording fee and the excise tax, and the office puts it on record. Electronic submission works too, because Guilford accepts every real estate document sent through its approved e-recording vendors.

E-recording returns the book and page data plus a stamped image within minutes, and the system rejects a document immediately if it misses the state's recording standards. Paper filings must also show where to send the original after recording. A standard document needs:

  • Letter or legal size paper, one-sided, black type on white stock.
  • Three blank inches above the text on page one, and a quarter inch of margin elsewhere.
  • Type no smaller than 9 point, with the instrument's title printed as a heading on the first sheet.
  • Pen entries for blanks and corrections are acceptable.

A document that fails any item draws the non-standard surcharge on top of the regular fee, so check the layout before you send it.

A general instrument of up to 15 pages starts at $26, and a mortgage or deed of trust of up to 35 pages starts at $64. Each page past those limits adds $4. State law fixes those amounts, and the county's table adds the smaller line items.

Guilford County recording and copy fees

An ordinary copy of a real estate record is 5 cents a page at the counter and $1 by mail. These statutory fees are the only ones allowed, and payment comes first.

A few extras come up around a sale. A notary oath costs $10, and authenticating a notary costs $1 per notary per page. A map copy is 50 cents, and certified plats are $5 per copy. UCC filings run $38, or $45 above two pages plus $2 for each page past ten. Guilford takes only fixture-related UCC filings, and every other UCC filing goes to the Secretary of State in Raleigh.

sections.h2: Who pays the deed excise tax?
sections.html:
The transferor does, handing it to the register before the deed goes on record. State law sets the rate at $1 per $500 of the price, counting any leftover fraction as a full $500. Deeds since August 1, 1991 are shown at $2 per thousand, which is the same thing.

Half of the revenue stays in the county's general fund and the remainder is forwarded each month to the state revenue department. A closing statement lists the tax apart from the recording fee. Two older rate bands, $1 per thousand for 1968 through July 1991 and $1.10 per thousand before 1968, matter only when you read an old deed. For your own sale, get the exact figure from the closing attorney.

A loan stays visible against the title until someone records a satisfaction. North Carolina gives an unrecorded deed, option or long lease no priority over lien creditors or later buyers who paid value, and ranks competing claims by when they were registered.

There are three recordable forms of satisfaction, none of which costs anything to file:

  • A satisfaction signed by the secured creditor and acknowledged before a notary.
  • A trustee's or substitute trustee's satisfaction of the deed of trust.
  • An affidavit by a North Carolina attorney serving as satisfaction agent, for use when a lender never provides one.

The office no longer takes the original deed of trust and note as proof of payment. If an old lender's loan still shows open on your parcel, a recorded satisfaction clears it, and your attorney or the lender can arrange that.

Enroll in the Property Fraud Alert. It emails you when a document appears under a name variation you registered. The register must record a deed that meets the legal form once fees and taxes are paid, and the office does not test whether a signature is real.

Vacant or distressed homes, older owners and low-income owners are frequent targets. Warning signs include a transfer you never signed, tax bills that stop arriving, and a default notice on a home with no mortgage. If you find a bad deed, assemble the paperwork and report it to the Sheriff's Office or Greensboro or High Point police, the District Attorney, a real estate attorney and the register. The register cannot pull a recorded document from the index, so ask an attorney how to challenge it.

It also helps to check credentials, read contracts and consider a title search and title insurance.

sections.h2: Can a recorded deed be corrected?
sections.html:
Only indexing mistakes can be fixed by the office. G.S. 132-1.10 bars it from changing a recorded instrument, so a misspelled name, a faulty legal description or a wrong loan amount in the document itself needs a corrective instrument prepared by your attorney.

An Indexing Correction Request form handles cases where the index differs from the document. Call 336-641-7556 or use the office email with questions. The corrective instrument is recorded at the usual fees. The recording page also carries a Personal Information Redaction section and a Real Estate Document Request form for copies.

Pull your vesting deed and check the spelling of every name against your ID. Confirm every old loan has a recorded satisfaction. Ask your attorney whether a plat or easement affects the lot. On closing day the seller's excise tax is paid and the deed is recorded, usually electronically. A cash sale skips a lender's review, but the recording and the tax stay the same. For the tax side of a sale, read our Guilford County property tax guide.
Guilford has 246,403 housing units. About 59.9% of occupied homes are owner-occupied, the middle owned home is worth $259,900, and median gross rent is $1,163. Builders drew 2,876 permits in 2025.

faqs.q: Which phone number reaches Guilford's register of deeds?
faqs.a: 336-641-7556, for the Greensboro office at 201 W. Market St. and the High Point office at 325 E. Russell Ave., Room 155. Staff are available on weekdays, 8 a.m. until 5 p.m.

faqs.q: What does a Guilford deed filing cost?
faqs.a: Expect $26 for an instrument of up to 15 pages and $4 for each page past that, plus a $25 surcharge when the document is non-standard. The seller also pays the excise tax before recording.

faqs.q: Is e-recording available through the Guilford register?
faqs.a: Yes. The office takes all electronically submitted real estate documents via approved vendors, sends back the recording details and a stamped image within minutes, and flags documents that miss the state standards.

faqs.q: Does the Guilford register verify a deed's authenticity?
faqs.a: No. A deed that meets the format rules is recorded once fees and taxes are paid. Owners can sign up for the free Property Fraud Alert and report forgeries to law enforcement and the District Attorney.

faqs.q: Do satisfactions of a mortgage carry a Guilford recording fee?
faqs.a: No. Satisfactions, affidavits of satisfaction and trustee's satisfactions are filed free of charge. The office does not accept the original deed of trust and note in their place.
